blockers.title: Calling the post-kexec kernel outside the bind does not produce the closed host-ABI TCB DR-126 requires
evidence: The carried source requires the signed closure to declare the platform base/host-ABI TCB, cover every permitted OS ABI with a closed allowlist and identity rule, refuse undeclared resolution or identity drift, and prove on hostile clean machines that no ambient system dependency enters silently.

v30 truthfully changes the observed subject to firmware-launched-kernel-package, but then says a different kernel M entered by later kexec is outside this bind and is not a pass/fail cell. M is nevertheless the kernel implementing the host ABI for the qualification process; it is an actual OS-ABI TCB member, not merely a limitation on the label used for K.

NT-TCB-DISCLOSE-KEXEC explicitly says Not a pass/fail cell. g22.doesNotClaim simultaneously calls the limitation not a skipped NT-TCB cell. Those statements cannot both discharge NT-TCB-1..4: no test observes or refuses an undeclared M, so the hostile-clean-machine property is neither passed nor made inapplicable.

A machine can boot allowlisted K, preserve the signed transcript and quote, kexec an undeclared M, and still satisfy the firmware-launched K observation. The narrowed subject avoids falsely naming K as current, but the same machine is allowed to qualify a purported closed Linux host-ABI TCB that omits M.

Linux remains in D-002 slice 1 and v30 does not make post-kexec state a machine-level refusal. Disclosure therefore functions as an unrecorded Linux execution-path deferral rather than closure of the mandatory OS-ABI member.
blockers.impact: The platform TCB can qualify while the actual kernel host ABI is absent from the allowlist and unchecked. That violates the defining DR-126 closure and hostile-clean-machine properties even though the narrower observation is linguistically honest.
blockers.requiredRepair: At qualification, either authenticate the currently executing kernel and join it to a permitted OS-ABI entry, or prove and enforce that replacement cannot occur from the measured launch through qualification. A machine on which a different kernel has entered must refuse unless that current kernel is independently observed and allowlisted. A disclosure-only non-test cannot substitute for the required host-ABI negative test.

blockers.title: measuredBootTranscript is called signed but has no location or join in the exhaustive signed-carrier schema
evidence: measuredBootTranscript locks only a list shape and asserts that a concrete list is REQUIRED in the signed TCB inventory. It defines no carrier path, canonical serialization, transcript digest, signature/reference, platformProfileKey, subject association, or equality from a retained runtime transcript reference to signed carrier bytes.

The signedEntry schema is exhaustively exactly four fields. PLATFORM-ATTESTED.signedForm is extras-rejected as exactly {authenticityCore, optional sonameAbi}; PATHLESS-PLATFORM-ATTESTED.signedObject contains only tag plus pathlessObservation; and the package-db subject is extras-rejected as {kind,name,version,digest}. None has a measuredBootTranscript slot or digest reference.

measuredBootBind retains eventLog and a prose measuredBootTranscriptMatch, but not the transcript, a content digest, or the identity of the signed inventory member supplying it. tcbCarrier names the inventory field and verifiedInstallRoot but no transcript side table or binding key.

Concrete transcripts are deferred as G22 evidence while the contract claims to lock their shape. G22 evidence is not automatically a field of the signed runtime carrier, and the exact signed-entry grammar prevents a later population packet from adding the missing member without changing this contract.

A permissive verifier can accept any prover-supplied list that mirrors the untrusted log, restoring the eventType relabeling and code/config exemption of PTCB-V29-B3. A strict verifier has no signed transcript to select and must reject every Linux event. Merely using the adjective signed does not decide between them.
blockers.impact: The central type+order+digest repair has no cryptographic custody or subject association. It therefore cannot authenticate eventType or authorize the config-bearing exemption, and Linux either falsely allows an attacker-chosen transcript or is unsatisfiable.
blockers.requiredRepair: Add one exact signed-carrier location and canonical serialization for concrete transcripts, keyed to the complete platformProfile and the exact OS-ABI signed entry or subject. Bind its digest/reference inside an existing lawful signed field or revise the exhaustive signed schema explicitly. Retain that reference in measuredBootBind and require byte-for-byte or digest equality to the selected signed transcript before any row type is used. Define uniqueness and cross-entry substitution refusal.

shouldFix.title: runtimeContinuity is simultaneously optional hardening and a mandatory interval proof
evidence: runtimeContinuity.role now says HARDENING only, not an interval proof, and says absence does not by itself refuse when the firmware-launched subject and transcript match.

The same object's lockdown and kexecLoadDisabled members still say absence refuses. enforcedBootPolicy.runtimeContinuity still says This is the post-boot interval constraint and Unavailable indicators refuse this machine.

The append-only whatThisDoesNotDo array still says runtimeContinuity is the interval constraint, while newer entries disclaim current-kernel detection. No precedence rule demotes the contradictory live clauses.
shouldFix.impact: Validators disagree whether missing indicators qualify, and the artifact still presents disproven present-state reads as an interval proof in two normative locations. This causes over-refusal and defeats the claimed honesty repair.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Choose one standing. For the narrowed subject, make runtimeContinuity explicitly optional hardening everywhere, remove all absence-refuses and interval-proof language, and define only which contradictory present values may fail closed. Supersede or replace the stale whatThisDoesNotDo sentence rather than appending an opposite assertion.

shouldFix.title: The preferred RPM extraction step still uses the closed snapFd
evidence: archiveSnapshot closes snapFd and mandates that headerBind, digest, verify, and extract use only roFd. preferredApi.open, headerBind, digest, hold, and verify were corrected to roFd.
preferredApi.extract.on remains exactly snapFd after verify and lseek 0, even though digest says use of snapFd after close refuses and cliInheritedFd says snapFd is closed and MUST NOT be consumed.
authenticatedManifest.builtFrom in the same extraction object says roFd, leaving two different descriptors for one selected operation.
shouldFix.impact: The selected librpm path either dereferences a closed descriptor and rejects all RPM profiles or silently ignores one live clause. PTCB-V29-S2 is not completely repaired.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Replace preferredApi.extract.on with roFd after verify and lseek 0, then verify that no post-transition operation names snapFd.

shouldFix.title: recomputeDigest is not wired consistently into preKernelReferences and its input bytes are not retained
evidence: The new recomputeDigest.rule correctly requires recomputeDigest(eventType, preimageBytes) to equal the event digest and row.recomputedDigest. The live preKernelReferences.join still requires recomputedDigest == eventPreimage(event), an undefined legacy operation after eventPreimage was reduced to rule and unknownTypeRefuses.

preKernelReferences.form retains only {pcrIndex,globalLogIndex,eventType,recomputedDigest,signedEntry}. It has no preimageBytes or authenticated content reference. measuredBootTranscript likewise retains only the final digest.

Only kernelEvent has exact PE bytes through authenticatedKernelMember. Other PE drivers/applications, firmware blobs, POST regions, IPL, and non-host code are not supplied as bytes by the retained row; their signedEntry may bind only a digest. A verifier cannot independently perform the mandatory recomputation from the declared evidence.
shouldFix.impact: Strict verification cannot execute the code-bearing recomputation, while permissive implementations can treat a claimed recomputedDigest as proof. The v29 digest-algebra repair remains under-specified at the retained-evidence boundary.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Replace the legacy eventPreimage(event) equality with the exact recomputeDigest equality. For every type, retain the canonical preimage bytes or a uniquely authenticated content-addressed object from which they are read, with an equality to the transcript row and signedEntry. If signed digest equality intentionally replaces byte recomputation for a class, say so and remove the impossible recompute requirement for that class.

shouldFix.title: The ACTION and VARIABLE preimage serializations do not reproduce the TCG event bytes they name
evidence: ACTION defines preimageBytes as a UCS-2-LE action string. The TCG PC Client action-event payload for strings such as Calling EFI Application from Boot Option is an 8-bit action string; changing it to two-byte code units produces a different SHA-256. The clause also omits an exact length/terminator rule.

VARIABLE calls its bytes UEFI_VARIABLE_DATA but parenthetically serializes only UnicodeName || VariableData. The named structure also carries the variable GUID and explicit name/data lengths; omitting their encodings does not reproduce the measured structure and leaves endianness/width undefined.
The generic phrase as specified by TCG PFP supplies no pinned edition or specificationGoverns rule that overrides these conflicting explicit byte descriptions.
shouldFix.impact: Standard firmware action and variable events fail recomputeDigest, including BootCurrent, Boot####, SecureBoot, PK, KEK, db, and dbx. Different validators can also choose the explicit shortcut or the named structure.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Pin the governing TCG PC Client PFP edition and specify the exact Event/EventSize bytes for EV_EFI_ACTION. For UEFI_VARIABLE_DATA, serialize every field in its specified order, width, endianness, and character count, including GUID and both lengths. Add byte-level digest vectors for the fixed action and each required variable class.

shouldFix.title: Skipping every EV_NO_ACTION still omits StartupLocality replay semantics
evidence: v30 correctly stops extending ordinary EV_NO_ACTION rows, but replayAlgorithm still initializes every selected PCR to 32 zero bytes and gives no StartupLocality interpretation.

A TCG StartupLocality EV_NO_ACTION record is non-extending yet supplies the locality-dependent PCR-0 initial replay state. Treating it as an inert row after unconditional zero initialization reconstructs the wrong PCR-0 value for such boots.
evNoActionVector reserves only a vector proving the PCR is unchanged by the row. That is insufficient for the StartupLocality class explicitly left open by PTCB-V29-S3's required repair.
shouldFix.impact: Valid TPM2 event logs with StartupLocality over-refuse because PCR0 cannot match the quote, despite the claimed EV_NO_ACTION repair.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Distinguish ordinary no-action records from the defined StartupLocality event, validate its exact event data, and set the PCR0 replay initial value according to the pinned TCG rule. Include both ordinary and StartupLocality vectors.

shouldFix.title: The transcript-authenticated type rule has no transcript row for the PCR-7 facts that establish Secure Boot trust
evidence: eventPreimage.rule says the eventType selecting a grammar MUST come from measuredBootTranscript at that pcrSequenceIndex, not an unauthenticated log label.

measuredBootTranscript.covers only PCR 0,1,2,4 through the first PCR-4 separator. secureBootEvents are PCR-7 EV_EFI_VARIABLE_DRIVER_CONFIG rows for SecureBoot, PK, KEK, db, and dbx, and their values select whether K's signature and dbx status pass.

No PCR-7 transcript or separate signed type+order+digest policy exists. A strict verifier therefore has no transcript-authenticated type for recomputeDigest; a permissive verifier must fall back to the raw PCR-7 eventType, contradicting the central v30 rule.
shouldFix.impact: The Secure Boot/db trust branch is either non-executable or reintroduces unauthenticated event-type semantics for security-critical PCR-7 metadata.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Extend the signed transcript/policy to every PCR-7 event whose metadata is used, with the same type+order+digest and subject association, or define an equally authenticated separate PCR-7 transcript. Then apply the exact variable preimage serialization before using SecureBoot, db, or dbx.

verdictBasis: REJECT: 2 blockers and 6 SHOULD-FIX findings. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
conclusion: REJECT. v30 honestly narrows the Linux subject, extends the expected transcript through the PCR-4 separator, separates single-hash recomputation, repairs most roFd uses, and skips ordinary EV_NO_ACTION. It still does not close the actual host-ABI TCB after kexec, and the transcript that is supposed to authenticate event type has no lawful signed-carrier location or subject join. Runtime hardening has contradictory standing; one RPM extraction field still uses snapFd; code preimages are not retained or consistently joined; action/variable bytes are wrong or incomplete; StartupLocality remains undefined; and PCR-7 security facts are outside the transcript. DR-126 remains OPEN; Linux remains D-002 slice 1; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, application, sealing, or implementation authority is created.
